record.context_brief: form-factor treatment of a two-constriction quantum Hall interferometer
record.original_question: For a quantum Hall bar interferometer with two constrictions, where the tunneling Hamiltonian contains two cosine terms with amplitudes γ1 and γ2 and the observable is the tunneling current as a function of magnetic flux Φ0 and constriction separation d, how can a form-factor method compute the relevant current-current correlators when the usual odd/even field transformation no longer decouples the fields for two constrictions?

evidence.quote: Chamon et al [cond-mat/9607195] discussed the device based on the quantum Hall bar with two constrictions which allows observation of interesting interference effects.

The quantity of interest is the tunelling current It(Φ0, d) as a function of flux Φ0 and distance d. For the current It it is sufficient to take its linear response limit, given by Kubo’s formula. The current-current correlators can be obtained using form-factors method and treating one of the cosine terms in (53) as a perturbation of integrable sine-Gordon model.
In the second problem the usual trick of changing the basis of fields to the odd and even fields does not work with two constrictions. The odd and even fields are not decoupled any longer.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a quantum Hall bar interferometer with two point-contact constrictions located a distance $d$ apart, with magnetic flux $\Phi_0$ threading the enclosed region. Model the two chiral edges by a pair of chiral bosonic fields, and take the tunneling Hamiltonian to be a sum of two local cosine (vertex-operator) backscattering terms at the two constrictions,
$$H_{\mathrm{tun}} = \gamma_1 \cos\bigl(\beta\,\phi(x_1)\bigr) + \gamma_2 \cos\bigl(\beta\,\phi(x_2) + \alpha(\Phi_0,d)\bigr),$$
where $\alpha$ encodes the Aharonov–Bohm phase depending on $\Phi_0$ and the constriction separation $d$, and $\beta$ is the Luttinger parameter fixed by the filling fraction. Let $I_t(\Phi_0,d)$ denote the tunneling current, computed in the Kubo linear-response limit from current–current correlation functions of $H_{\mathrm{tun}}$.

For a single constriction, the standard change of variables to "odd" and "even" linear combinations of the two edge fields decouples the Hamiltonian into a free chiral sector and a boundary sine–Gordon sector, allowing exact computation of the current–current correlator via the form-factor expansion of the integrable sine–Gordon model (treating the cosine as the integrable perturbation). With two constrictions, this odd/even change of basis no longer decouples the fields, because the two cosine terms involve the fields at two distinct spatial points.

Problem: Develop a form-factor based method that computes the current–current correlators, and hence $I_t(\Phi_0,d)$, for this two-constriction Hamiltonian. Concretely, treat one of the two cosine terms as a perturbation of the integrable sine–Gordon model defined by the other cosine, and produce a tractable form-factor expansion (with explicit matrix elements and a controlled series) for the linear-response tunneling current as a function of $\Phi_0$ and $d$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returns work on two-constriction (Fabry–Pérot) quantum Hall interferometers and boundary sine–Gordon mappings, including recent multi-site mesoscopic treatments, but no source providing a complete form-factor expansion of the current–current correlator for the two-constriction interferometer in the regime where the odd/even decoupling fails. The status of a fully worked form-factor solution is not clearly established by the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Tunneling in multi-site mesoscopic quantum Hall circuits
status_evidence.snippet: Transport properties of the single- and two-site mesoscopic quantum Hall circuits at high transparencies can be described in terms of the lowest-order backscattering perturbations, and mapping to the boundary sine-Gordon model can be exploited.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work still treats two-constriction circuits via boundary sine-Gordon mappings perturbatively, not by an exact form-factor solution.

status_evidence.title: Theory of the Fabry-Perot quantum Hall interferometer
status_evidence.snippet: Interference oscillations can be observed in the tunneling current as a function of Aharonov-Bohm phase, with dependence on edge-mode velocities and interactions.
status_evidence.claim: Two-constriction interferometer current is studied with various edge-theory methods but a full form-factor computation in the non-decoupling regime is not standard.
